QF.id: Clubbing, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses_22

question.text: Mr. Prakash transferred property worth Rs.20,00,000 to his HUF (Hindu Undivided Family). The property generates rental income of Rs.1,80,000 per year. How is this income treated for tax purposes?

answer.text: HUF's income under Section 22, as the property now belongs to the HUF
Clubbed with Prakash's income under Section 64, as income from property gifted to HUF is included in the transferor's total income
Split between Prakash and HUF in proportion to their respective shares
Exempt from tax as transfers to HUF are not treated as transfers

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the Section 64 clubbing provisions, income from property gifted to an HUF is clubbed with the transferor's total income under the same head as it would have been taxed in the HUF. The rental income of Rs.1,80,000 is therefore included in Prakash's total income. The Trap: Option A is a common error — once the property sits with the HUF, students assume the income belongs to the HUF. The clubbing rule specifically catches this. Note: The clubbed income retains its character and is taxed in the transferor's hands under the same head.
